learning: Check s-bend and slalom progress against iteration 4 (0.127 and 0.093) and iteration 5 (0.132 and 0.091). If progress is unchanged, body_length is not a lever and the next step is mass alone. Report per-track values, and oval steering_oscillation against 0.25.
notes: Complete robot: Builder's geometry (track 0.10, body 0.10 x 0.12, mass 0.6) with the iteration 4 controller unchanged. The aim is to isolate the body and mass change.
rationale: The Builder's geometry (track 0.10 m, body_length 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg) combines two changes from the best-supported recent points. Iteration 4 (track 0.10, body 0.12, mass 0.7) kept line loss at zero, held rms_error near 0.02 and gave an oval finish rate of 65%, but the s-bend and slalom still ended off_track at max_error about 0.062 with progress 0.127 and 0.093. Iteration 5 (track 0.09, mass 0.6) raised s-bend progress only to 0.132, and the oval finish rate fell to 35%, so narrowing the track below 0.10 m is not worth repeating. I keep the sensor array (x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, y 0.05, 0.016 m footprint), wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m unchanged. The controller is kept identical to iteration 4 (kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.5, weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], last_direction) so that the race isolates the body and mass change. The contract says body_length has no direct dynamics effect, which conflicts with the Builder's yaw-inertia reasoning, so the s-bend and slalom progress will show which applies. Expected result: oval finish rate at or above 55%, and s-bend or slalom progress above 0.13 with max_error near 0.06 m.
